_source: Placement library (4/N). The 8 Ashtakoota factors keyed by slug. Lets the matching reading explain WHY a koota scored what it did — previously LLM-only, which is how a deterministic 36-point calculation ended up with a non-deterministic explanation. Payload { name, maxPoints, text, lowScoreNote }. English-authored; run `npm run kb:backfill -- --tables=koota-meaning`.
_shape: { name: string, maxPoints: number, text: string, lowScoreNote: string }

en.name: Varna
en.text: Compares the spiritual/temperamental grade of the two Moon signs. Worth 1 point — the smallest factor, and a zero here is routinely overridden by the rest of the chart.
en.lowScoreNote: A zero means the groom's varna sits below the bride's. Traditionally noted, rarely decisive on its own.

en.name: Vashya
en.text: Measures mutual magnetism — who naturally influences whom. Worth 2 points, and speaks to the balance of power in the relationship.
en.lowScoreNote: A low score suggests one partner will tend to lead and the other to follow; workable when both accept it.

en.name: Tara
en.text: Compares birth nakshatras for mutual auspiciousness, indicating health and fortune for the couple. Worth 3 points.
en.lowScoreNote: A low Tara points to periods of strain around health or luck; remedial timing (muhurat) is the classical response.

en.name: Yoni
en.text: Physical and instinctive compatibility, drawn from the animal symbol of each birth nakshatra. Worth 4 points.
en.lowScoreNote: A low Yoni indicates differing physical rhythms and needs — usually a matter of communication rather than incompatibility.

en.name: Graha Maitri
en.text: Friendship between the lords of the two Moon signs — mental and intellectual rapport. Worth 5 points and one of the most meaningful factors day to day.
en.lowScoreNote: A low score suggests the two minds work differently. Genuine affection can still bridge it, but it takes conscious effort.

en.name: Gana
en.text: Temperament grouping — Deva (gentle), Manushya (balanced) or Rakshasa (intense). Worth 6 points and a strong indicator of everyday harmony.
en.lowScoreNote: A Deva-Rakshasa mismatch is the classic friction pattern: one partner reads the other as harsh, the other reads them as fragile.

en.name: Bhakoot
en.text: The distance between the two Moon signs, governing prosperity and family welfare. Worth 7 points.
en.lowScoreNote: A zero (Bhakoot dosha) is taken seriously in tradition, but is considered cancelled when Graha Maitri is strong or the Moon-sign lords are the same.

en.name: Nadi
en.text: The largest single factor at 8 points, relating to constitutional type (Vata/Pitta/Kapha) and, classically, progeny.
en.lowScoreNote: A zero is Nadi dosha — the most weighted objection in Guna Milan. It is regarded as cancelled when both share a Moon sign, or the Moon-sign lords are identical, or the nakshatra is the same but the pada differs.
